description: Transparent weighted-sum risk model. Every feature is normalised to 0-1 with an explicit piecewise-linear curve, multiplied by a configurable weight, and summed to a 0-100 score. This is a decision-support heuristic, NOT a calibrated or validated hydrological flood forecast.
methodology_note: Rainfall breakpoints follow India Meteorological Department rainfall intensity classes where applicable (IMD defines a cloudburst as rainfall exceeding 100 mm in one hour). Terrain and hydrology breakpoints are engineering judgement chosen to spread real observed values across the 0-1 range, and are configurable.

rainfall_intensity.label: Rainfall intensity
rainfall_intensity.rationale: Short-duration rainfall intensity is the dominant trigger of flash flooding in steep catchments. The 100 mm/h endpoint is the IMD cloudburst threshold.

rainfall_3h.label: 3-hour rainfall accumulation
rainfall_3h.rationale: Captures burst totals over the typical response time of a small Himalayan catchment.

rainfall_24h.label: 24-hour rainfall accumulation
rainfall_24h.rationale: Breakpoints correspond to IMD daily rainfall classes: moderate, heavy, very heavy and extremely heavy rainfall.

rainfall_forecast_24h.label: Forecast rainfall (next 24 h)
rainfall_forecast_24h.rationale: Forward-looking component. Gives lead time rather than only reporting what has already fallen.

rainfall_trend.label: Rainfall trend
rainfall_trend.rationale: An intensifying storm is more dangerous than a decaying one at the same instantaneous intensity.

rainfall_anomaly.label: Rainfall anomaly vs local climatology
rainfall_anomaly.rationale: Computed from ERA5 reanalysis history for the same location and calendar window. 60 mm is unremarkable in one valley and a record in another; the percentile makes the signal locally meaningful.

antecedent_precipitation_index.label: Soil saturation (antecedent precipitation index)
antecedent_precipitation_index.rationale: API is a standard hydrological proxy for catchment wetness, computed as the decay-weighted sum of previous daily rainfall. Saturated ground converts a far larger fraction of new rainfall into surface runoff.

slope.label: Terrain slope
slope.rationale: Derived by finite-difference gradient on sampled Copernicus DEM elevations. Steep slopes shorten the time to peak discharge and enable debris flow.

terrain_relief.label: Local terrain relief
terrain_relief.rationale: Elevation range within the sampled neighbourhood. High relief concentrates runoff into narrow valley floors.

river_proximity.label: Proximity to river network
river_proximity.rationale: True point-to-polyline distance to the nearest OpenStreetMap waterway. Closer to the channel means less warning time and greater inundation depth.

stream_density.label: Stream network density
stream_density.rationale: Drainage density measured from OpenStreetMap waterway geometry. Denser networks deliver runoff to the outlet faster.

river_discharge_anomaly.label: River discharge anomaly
river_discharge_anomaly.rationale: Current GloFAS modelled river discharge divided by the location's own recent mean discharge. An independent hydrological signal that does not come from the rainfall feed.

impact_thresholds.note: A contributor's impact label is based on its share of the total raw weighted score.

confidence_rules.note: Confidence describes DATA QUALITY, not the probability of a flood. It degrades when sources are missing, stale or simulated.
